titel: Messages: for you, read along, sent
kurz: Everything you write to agents and everything they write to you is in one place – from all projects on this PC together. Every line shows its project with a colour mark; at the top you pick “All projects” or a single one. Notices from the Workbench itself show “System” as the sender. For each recipient you see how far a message has got – and as long as nobody has read it, you can withdraw it.
brauchst: The Workbench at the PC or the online site. Menu › Messages.

schritte.text: Messages › “+ Write” – pick a recipient (one agent or everyone), type, text. From an agent (“Message”) the recipient is already filled in.

Wherever you look at something – topic, milestone, decision, run, review – there is “✉ Message about this”: the reference is filled in and a recipient suggested (you can change it). Topics and milestones show “Messages about this” below as a small conversation. For tasks and documents you keep writing in their own field – that carries the reference too.
“Sent” tab: per recipient sent › notified › read › done. Hover over a step to see the time.

Clicking a message shows the whole thread on the right, as in a mail program: everything with the same reference (or in the same reply chain), including what agents wrote to each other about it – oldest at the top, the chosen message outlined. The list shows “· n in thread”. Long threads show the last 30 first (“Show older”). On a phone it opens as its own view (“‹ For you” returns).

The “For you” tab first shows only unread messages (“unread only” is on); at the top “n to do for you” counts all projects. Unread is bold. Tapping opens it and marks it as read – it stays in the list until you leave the page, but no longer counts. “Reply” writes back, the reference comes along; “Done” marks the one shown, “All done” all open ones – like `amw erledigt`, also online and on the phone.
Sent › pick a message › “Withdraw” – as long as **no** recipient has read or done it. It disappears for every recipient and stays with you as “withdrawn”.

fehler: A message stays at “sent” for a long time
The agent is not running, or it is a chat lead that only reads on its own rhythm. The start page shows whether it is running.
A recipient has already read it. Send a new message (“please ignore”).
Messages via “+ Write” in the menu are general; write via “✉ Message about this” on the item and it comes along.
danach: Questions to you are only under the “Questions” menu item – with follow-up questions, additions and your answer. Messages only shows a note at the top saying how many are open.

Only the lead (and the co-developer) asks you. If another agent asks, the question goes to the lead: the lead settles it or asks you – then as the lead's own question, reworked first or bundled with others; who asked originally is shown in the history. Tasks and questions sent to you as messages also go to the lead first; info (e.g. “live”) still comes straight to you.
Every line shows its kind: ✉ message from an agent, ⚙ notice from the Workbench. To mark several open ones as done at once: tick them (or “select all unread”), then “Done”.
What agents and lead write to each other is under “Read along” – from all projects, read only, it never counts.
The Overview shows only a card with the newest messages for you – one click takes you to “For you”. The number in the menu is for the chosen project, “n to do for you” on the page for all.
On the PC the list and the message scroll separately, as in a mail program: you can read on the right without losing the list.
fragen: **sent** – the message is in AMW. **notified** – the service has woken the agent (chat leads read on their next round). **read** – the agent has fetched it with `amw lesen`. **done** – it has dealt with it. **being sent …** – online only, until the PC has taken it over.
What counts as a message to you?

Only what you need to act on: questions, review requests and tasks for you, answers to your messages, and AMW messages that need something from you (for example “ready for acceptance” or “drive is getting full”). Infos and reports stay readable but do not count. “Ready for acceptance” disappears by itself once the milestone no longer is. The lead learns that a priority run has been waiting long or a package is stuck.
When does the AMW notify an agent?

For orders, questions, answers, approvals, review requests and reports – never for an info; that only sits in the inbox and is seen at the next read. If the agent is working right now, the AMW waits until its next stop and then sends everything together as one notification. That saves cost. Immediately, even in the middle of work, only stop, corrections and everything you write yourself get through.
And if the lead does not react?

If the lead got a notification but has not read the message after 10 minutes and has written nothing since, the AMW wakes them once more – at most once per message. If an agent asks the lead for something (merge OK, review, approval, decision), it has to send it as a question; as an info the AMW refuses it, because an info does not wake.
Who learns that a state can be approved?

If a full test run ends green on exactly the state the reviewer marked green, the AMW tells the reviewer “freigabereif” by itself, with the ready command for the merge OK. If the full run is red, reviewer and builder are told.
How does a reply end up in the right conversation?
When an agent writes only to you, its reply attaches itself to your last unanswered message to it (up to 2 days old) and inherits its reference.
